senses: Within the urinary bladder.
A style of art that emphasises extreme simplicity of form.
A style of music that emphasises extreme simplicity of rhythms and melodic forms to achieve a trancelike effect.
Of simple living, the intentional reduction of material possessions and distractions.
A person who laminates.
A device that laminates.
A filtering machine operated by air pressure.
Describing the year of a monarch's reign starting from the date of accession.
ety: From Medieval Latin rēgnālis, from Latin rēgnum + -ālis.

senses: An Italian style of ice cream dessert made with layers of different colors and flavors (typically cherry, pistachio, and vanilla or chocolate) and usually containing candied fruits and nuts.
ety: From Italian spumoni, plural of spumone, from spuma (“foam”).

senses: A device that foams or froths liquid.
A screw-top culinary device that comprises a pressure vessel used to hold a liquid and is charged with a compressed gas, to force the contents out of the nozzle, to create a foam.
ety: From foam + -er. Foamers are called so because they foam at the mouth with awe

senses: A form of experimental folk music influenced by industrial music.
Such an injection
The principle that objects are equal if and only if their observed properties are the same, regardless of internal processes that lead to those properties.
The principle that functions are equal if and only if they operate on the same domain and for any given element of the domain the result of each of the functions is the same.
Merry; playful.
ety: From Italian giocoso, from Latin iocōsus.

senses: Synonym of parfum (“solvent containing around 15% to 40% aromatic compounds”).
A transition area between two adjacent ecological communities (ecosystems).
ety: Combination of eco- (“ecology”) + -tone, from the Greek τόνος (tónos, “tension”).

senses: A rice paddy.
without a bit (piece of metal in a horse's mouth).
Synonym of uppy (“the act of being held up”).
examples: When Daddy Gives Me Uppies When Daddy gives me uppies / Then I soar just like a plane, / It's bad I weigh five hundred pounds, / But good he has a crane.

senses: A very flexible horned serpent in Greek legend, said to have no spine and to hide its head in the sand awaiting prey.
Able to be integrated.
ety: From French intégrable, equivalent to integr(ate) + -able.

senses: Any time close to noon; midday or thereabouts.
Divided into a hundred parts.
Describing a hundredth part.
Someone who belches.
Something resembling a (wheat) sheaf in appearance.
A kind of ornamental firework.
ety: Late 16th century, borrowed from French gerbe (“sheaf”). Doublet of garb.

senses: The extent to which something is incomparable.
An amount that fills or covers the face.
examples: Because l didn't dare take either hand off the wheel, I did get a few facefuls of snow, passing under hemlocks with especially low-drooped branches, but that was a cheap price for getting the tractor safely out.

senses: Able to be read using a certain set of reading knowledge.
capable of being decoded
examples: Decodable books are sold in packs, with more letter combinations appearing in each successive book.

senses: Tending to trot; having a trotting gait.
A ball-shaped Japanese dumpling made of batter and filled with diced octopus, tempura scraps, pickled ginger, and green onion.
examples: There is fresh fish and lotus root and an abundance of other options, such as dumplings (four for 50 pesos) or Japanese takoyakis, fried octopus balls (six for 100 pesos).

senses: A former money of account in Portuguese India, one twentieth of a rupia.
ety: Borrowed from Portuguese pardao (an obsolete spelling of pardau), from Sanskrit प्रतापः (pratāpaḥ), which was written on the coins.

senses: Synonym of governorate.
ety: From govern + -ate (forms nouns denoting rank or office).
examples: The group met Friday morning and took a bus north from Cairo to the Qalyubiya governate, an hour away.

senses: The infliction of trauma; the act or process of traumatizing.
A dagger or poignard, especially the kind used by the Ancient Romans.
examples: The Pugio or Dagger was used by the Romans, a species of that weapon called the Hand Seax was worn by the Saxons, with which they massacred the English on Salisbury Plain in 476.

senses: A suede-like synthetic textile, composed of polyester and polyurethane.
ety: Probably derived from Italian Alcantara (“river in Italy”) or possibly Spanish Alcántara, both from Arabic اَلْقَنْطَرَة (al-qanṭara, “the bridge”). The reason for the derivation is unknown.
examples: The interior is trimmed in soft merino leather, in either off-white and brown or off-white and black, with hand-woven off-white piping and an alcantara synthetic suede head liner in off-white.

senses: Having pimples; pimpled.
Mechanically unreliable or in disrepair.
Shaped like a rocker; curving upwards at the ends.
Of footwear: having a rocker (a thicker-than-normal sole with a rounded heel).
Fitted with a rocker.
examples: Toning shoes have a rockered bottom to force you to roll up and over a hump under the foot, or in essence, fight up and over the shoe.

senses: A spearlike weapon with a barbed head used in hunting whales and large fish.
A sharp tip within a disposable syringe, used to penetrate the stopper.
ety: From Old French harpon, from Latin harpaga, a variant of Latin harpagō, from Ancient Greek ἁρπάγη (harpágē, “hook”), from ἁρπάζω (harpázō, “to snatch away, to carry off, to seize, to captivate”). Sense and spelling perhaps influenced by Dutch harpoen (“harpoon”). Doublet of harpagon.

senses: A juggling apparatus consisting of a spool which is whirled and tossed on a string attached to handsticks.
ety: Borrowed from French diabolo, from older diable (literally “devil”), fancifully altered after cognate Italian diavolo and/or their common source, Latin diabolus. First attested in the early 20th century. The Latin noun is from Ancient Greek διάβολος (diábolos, “devil”), itself derived from the verb διαβάλλω (diabállō, “to slander”, literally “to throw across”). senses: Containing its own meaning or purpose; deriving meaning and purpose from within.
Not motivated by anything beyond itself; thematically self-contained.
ety: From Ancient Greek αὐτός (autós, “self”) + τέλος (télos, “result; end”); compare auto- and telic. From early 20th century.

senses: Any system where one group has significantly more influence than another, such as when voting districts are unevenly spread out across a population (compare gerrymandering).
Any other soporific drug.
ety: From soporific. Sopor has been used as a brand name for methaqualone.
